concerns.text: Task T012 includes a fallback note: 'If CPU OOM occurs, the execution stage will auto-offload this specific script to a Kaggle GPU runner'. This violates Constitution Principle I (Reproducibility) which mandates runs on a 'fresh GitHub Actions runner' without external ad-hoc offloading. The task silently relaxes the constraint that the pipeline must be reproducible on the declared target platform (GitHub Actions Free Tier) by introducing an unverified external dependency.

Task T029 implements a statistical test against 'Aggregated baselines (T026b) and Static results'. However, the Spec FR-006 explicitly requires a 'paired t-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test to determine if the performance difference between the static heuristic and the learned sparse model (averaged over 5 seeds) is statistically significant'. The task description fails to explicitly mandate the *paired* nature of the test on document-level differences, risking a semantic weakening of the statistical validity required to falsify the hypothesis (Constitution Principle VI).

Tasks T028 and T028b implement 'Cross-Model Validation' on Gemma-2. While the Plan introduces this as a 'mandatory validation step', the Spec (FR-001 through FR-008) and Success Criteria (SC-001 through SC-005) contain no requirement or metric for cross-model validation. Introducing this work without a corresponding Spec requirement constitutes a silent drift from the defined scope and creates unmeasurable work (no SC-006 in Spec), violating the constraint that tasks must not introduce work not demanded by the spec.

Task T005 requires a unit test asserting 'peak memory usage < 7GB'. The Spec Assumption A6 and Plan 'Complexity Tracking' admit that generating full attention maps for long sequences is 'intractable' on 7GB RAM without a 'sampled subset' strategy. A unit test asserting a hard 7GB limit on the *data loader* without explicitly scoping the test to the 'sampled subset' logic (or mocking the data volume) creates a contradiction: the test will fail for realistic long-context inputs unless the test itself violates the 'real-call' nature of the data loader. The task weakens the requirement by not explicitly linking the memory constraint to the sampling strategy defined in the Plan.
